falsifier: Any shipped rule that stops replaying under the stricter model would show the omission was load-bearing rather than latent -- checked this run by forcing every webfrank edge to re-run (touch tools/gdl/webfrank.py; ninja -j2) and counting 257 WEBFRANK application lines with build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK. Re-run that to re-check. A second falsifier for the general form: a remaining opcode carrying Rc that is still unmodelled here -- grep `_word_effects` for the opcode sets and compare against the PowerPC M-form/X-form Rc-bearing lists.
subject: project:gdl
value: webfrank's `_word_effects` -- the single shared architectural-effect model behind the permutation dependence audit, the recolor bisimulation, the constant/zero dataflows and the dead-final-write proof -- did not model the Rc bit on the M-form rotates. It handled Rc for the opcode-31 forms and for opcodes 13/28/29, and silently omitted opcodes 20, 21 and 23, so `rlwinm.`, `rlwimi.` and `rlwnm.` read as writing ONLY their destination GPR. A permutation window could therefore have moved a record-setting rotate past a CR0 consumer with the dependence audit seeing no conflict at all, and the audit would have reported success. FIXED 2026-09-02 (`if opcode in (20, 21, 23) and word & 1: writes.add(("cr", 0))`); the change can only make every guard STRICTER, and all 257 pre-existing WebFrank rule applications re-ran green in the same build, so the gap was latent and not live. HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the transferable part: not by auditing the model, but by a NEW class's own whitelist test asserting that a record-setting variant must be refused for writing CR0 -- the assertion failed because the refusal never fired. A guard's acceptance is as much a measurement of the guard as its refusal is (the converse of discipline 14), and a new proof class is a cheap oracle for the shared machinery underneath it, because it exercises corners no shipped rule happens to sit on. Any lane adding a class to a shared model should write at least one test per REFUSAL its class promises, not only per acceptance.
